question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10}{\sqrt{r+2}-\sqrt{r+4}} & = \\ \frac{10}{\sqrt{r+2}-\sqrt{r+4}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4}}{\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4}} & = \\ \frac{10(\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4})}{(\sqrt{r+2}-\sqrt{r+4})(\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4})} & = \\ \frac{10(\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4})}{(\sqrt{r+2})^{2}-(\sqrt{r+4})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{10(\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4})}{(r+2)-(r+4)} & = \\ \frac{10(\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4})}{(-2)} & = \\ -5(\sqrt{r+2}+\sqrt{r+4})\end{aligned}
$$
